title: Maximilian I's diplomatic reports partly in cipher: Veit von Fürst (Rome, Bologna), Andrea de Burgo (Blois, Milan, Brussels), Paulus de Laude (Blois), Mercurino Gattinara (Seville), Giovanni Colla (Rome)

title: Hieronymus Łaski → Ferdinand I from Constantinople, ciphered letters of his last embassy to Süleyman

status: AIS: 'Chiffriertes Schreiben von Hieronymus Laski an Ferdinand I.'; no decipherment noted (other Türkei I items say 'interlinear dechiffriert' when glossed). The repo rebuilt Łaski's 1531 key to the Bavarian dukes (kaa4591) — a different alphabet but the same writer. Not on DECODE. || Brackx, issue #172 (28 Oct 2026): AIS notes 'interlinear dechiffriert' on Türkei I 5-2-1, 5-2-5, 5-2-7, 5-2-9 and 5-2-10; 5-1-77 glossed likewise; all printed in Gévay, Urkunden und Actenstücke III (Vienna 1842; archive.org urkundenundacten113gv), Beilagen 27-47. Read at the time and in print; more letters (5-2-18, 5-2-20 ...) are listed in the issue.
why: Łaski's 1540-41 mission, in which he was imprisoned by the Porte while Buda fell (1541): first-hand reports to Ferdinand.

title: Constantinople ciphers of Ferdinand I's resident Malvezzi and his circle: Veltwyck 1547, 'mehrere vollständig chiffrierte Briefe' 1548, Hungarian estates' letter 1547
correspondents: Giovanni Maria Malvezzi, Gerhard Veltwyck → Ferdinand I; Hungarian estates (exemplum); John Sigismund / Sigismund Augustus → Süleyman (intercepted copies)
shelfmark: HHStA Wien, StAbt Türkei I 7-1-4, 7-2-25, 7-3-39, 8-3-8, 8-3-11, 8-4-6, 9-1-8 (7-2-18 read elsewhere, see status)
status: AIS: 7-2-18 'Inhalt nicht dechiffriert'; 7-1-4 (Veltwyck) and 7-3-39 'vollständig chiffriert' with no decipherment; siblings 7-1-9 and 7-3-20 carry 'Dechiffrierung'. The repo read Ferdinand→Malvezzi 1548 (malvezzi1548, DECODE R366) — the same resident's cipher. Target malvezzi1548 holds a Malvezzi key (DECODE R367). 27 Oct 2026, Brice Dudout (Europe chiffrée, documents.html#huyson-1547): 7-2-18 (fols. 143r-146r, 207 lines) read, about 97.5% of some 1,550 groups, with Malvezzi's alphabet frozen and checked blind. It is Malvezzi's enciphered Latin copy of Henri II's letter of credence for d'Huyson to Süleyman and of two other letters of Henri II, with Malvezzi's Italian notes: the Swiss to be included in the truce, Charles V's letters 'lusorias et ridicolas'. Ribier (1666) prints the French content, not this text. Entry narrowed to the other files. Merged 27 Oct 2026 as targets/huyson1547 (pull request #136, write-up huyson1547.html).
why: Habsburg-Ottoman truce of 1547 and the Transylvanian crisis, from the imperial resident's own ciphers.

status: PARES title "Carta cifrada de García" to the Marquis of Villena or to his brother Alonso Téllez, probably 1475-1479. Reported by Brice Dudout (28 Oct 2026, after viewing the images): a code of cover words (badillo, granoso, hotalua ...) with short runs of symbols. He found no prior work in this repository, Tomokiyo, Lasry, DECODE or Galende 2013, and no known Castilian table of the period. Unread. Not viewed here.
why: A fifteenth-century Castilian cipher letter, earlier than 1497, so relevant to the oldest-cipher search; word-code plus symbols, which is not a common Castilian system of the time.

title: Alfonso Cistarelli (Kraków) to Duke Alfonso I d'Este, no. 7, in cipher (Vestigia V1908)
correspondents: Alfonso Cistarelli → Alfonso I d'Este
shelfmark: ASMo, Ambasciatori, Ungheria b. 4, Alfonso Cistarelli no. 7 (Vestigia V1908, DF 294963); not on DECODE
folio_note: original not seen; Vestigia reproduction only
status: Vestigia V1908, Cistarelli's seventh letter, 14 Oct 1520, in cipher. Reported by Brice Dudout (28 Oct 2026): neither on DECODE nor in this repository as far as he can see. His key for the Caprile/Cistarelli cipher reads part of it (one line so far). He has asked ASMo for the original. Not checked here. Attempted 28 Oct 2026 (targets/cistarelli1520/, joined to catalogue 158: same two-digit cipher as R1137): addressee Alfonso I and place Kraków per Vestigia and the clear text (reports Cardinal Ippolito's death); line 7 transcribed, R1137 anneal key gives fragments only; about six cipher lines at the foot lost in the photocopy. Needs the original.
why: Another letter in the same Eger cipher family as R1137 (25 Jul 1520, catalogue 158) and the Caprile letters; a new ciphertext, with a key that already partly fits.

title: Florence, letters to the Signoria in the cipher of 1414 (Gabbrielli's partial key, letters never read)
correspondents: unknown Florentine envoy or commissary → Signoria / Dieci di Balìa
shelfmark: ASF, Signori, Responsive originali, filza 1 (key: ASF Chiavi delle cifre II, pars 3 no. 1)
status: Meister 1902 p. 49 prints "Florenz, Beispiele 1: Cifra Decemviri di Balia 1414 (Lettere della Signoria risponsive; filza Nr. 1)", a partial homophonic alphabet Gabbrielli rebuilt in 1864 from glossed words (several letters blank; per = 8, et = f, che = dum). No sender or folio given; no reading of the letters printed (Guasti's Commissioni has nothing for 1414). The same situation as florence1429, where Gabbrielli's 1424 table read only glossed words. Session of 23 Sept 2026 (targets/florence1414/): key transcribed (KEY.md, 38 signs); 'filza 1' is an old number (today's Signori Responsive 1 is 1340), so the letters are probably in Signori Responsive 7-8 or Signori-Dieci-Otto, Legazioni e commissarie, missive e responsive 8; not on DECODE, Yale Ilardi reels or ASF PAD. Outgoing registers Legazioni e commissarie 5-6 (PAD) scanned: clear, no cipher; reg. 6 ff. ~35-52 are the 1414 instructions (candidate senders).
why: The oldest Florentine cipher letters; a full reading would beat the project's 1425 record by eleven years.

title: German Army Truppenschlüssel messages, net 'pz6', 4 July 1941 (Nr. 88, 90, 91, 92, 94, 97; also 95, 96 same day)
correspondents: German Army front-line units (call sign pz6) → same net
shelfmark: German Army message collection (original message forms, provenance given only as the German Army message collection; the BGAC page names the Bundesarchiv for its 2026 finds); transcribed by Olaf Ostwald and Frode Weierud
folio_note: Six pz6 messages 35+96+88+126+143+59 = 547 letters, plus Nr. 95 (74) and Nr. 96 (62) with blank addressee; facsimiles for Nr. 88, 94, 95
status: CryptoCellar 1941 Message List (status 20 Oct 2026) marks 24 of the 30 messages broken in Sept 2026 (Paefgen; Davies, Willis, Khan, marked AI), DOLHA 252 only in part; pz6 Nr. 88-97 by Paefgen 21.09 and Davies 25.09; plaintexts not published. Still unbroken: EHNPZ 123 (8 Jul, net 4fc), AFUVO 26, ZUBZE 8, MZXNX 21, AAXYN 31, AOXST 91; also BCUCC Nr. 20 NF (5 Sep 1941), not in this row. See targets/ts1941pz6/ (WAINUT, PR #125; ciphertext-only attempt failed; Status: no write-up). Earlier: Listed as unbroken on CryptoCellar 'Unbroken German Army Truppenschlüssel Messages' (updated 27 Jul 2026). Truppenschlüssel is a hand cipher (simplified Doppelkasten); most of the 100+ surviving TS messages were broken by Ostwald & Weierud (Cryptologia 2021). Not in the repo (only Enigma rows of this collection are on HCPortal; Cryptoole's CryptoCellar rows were dropped wholesale as Enigma). This entry covers all 30 unbroken 1941 Truppenschlüssel messages on the CryptoCellar list, by net: net 'pz6', 4 July 1941 (Nr. 88, 90, 91, 92, 94, 97; also 95, 96 same day); net 'nfw', 3 July 1941 (Nr. 84, 85, 86); net '4fc', 8 July 1941 (Nr. 123, 129, 130); net 'f8y', 6 and 8 July 1941 (Nr. 109, 110, 121); net '8be', 25 July 1941 (Nr. 263, 264); June-September 1941 (VHRNE Nr. 284, AOXST Nr. 91, XWFEC Nr. 193, MZXNX Nr. 21, AAXYN Nr. 31, DOLHA Nr. 252, LSSLG Nr. 268, ZUBZE Nr. 8, CFQIB Nr. 281, YSGSS Nr. 56, AFUVO Nr. 26). They were dropped from the 14 Oct Cryptoole import because research/cryptoole/pull.py filtered every CryptoCellar row as Enigma.
why: A same-day, same-net group of a WWII hand field cipher left unbroken by modern cryptanalysis: a direct test case for the paper beside the Orpo Doppelkasten target.
